edges.description: Without ALG8 the lipid-linked precursor is incompletely glucosylated, so polycystin-1 is hypoglycosylated and less of it reaches a mature, endoglycosidase H-resistant form.
Immature polycystin-1 fails to traffic past the Golgi to the plasma membrane and the primary cilium.
Glycosylation failure also activates the IRE1-alpha/XBP1 arm of the unfolded protein response.
edges.target: Endoplasmic Reticulum Unfolded Protein Response Activation

edges.description: Reduced functional polycystin-1 in tubular epithelium leads to cyst formation through the polycystin pathway shared with PKD1.
The same polycystin-1 deficit in cholangiocytes drives biliary-derived liver cysts.
Complete local loss of ALG8 in biliary epithelium would remove the remaining polycystin-1 maturation capacity in that clone.
edges.source: Somatic Second Hit in Cyst Epithelium

edges.description: Renal cystogenesis produces bilateral kidney cysts.
A minority of clinically ascertained carriers have reduced eGFR; how much of it is due to the cysts rather than modifiers or comorbidity is unresolved.
Kidney stones were more frequent in carriers in the Geisinger cohort; the link to cysts is inferred from the parallel with ADPKD.
Hepatic cystogenesis produces polycystic liver disease.
Cyst burden enlarges the liver in a minority.
Abdominal pain was the most common presenting complaint; it is attributed to cyst burden by analogy with ADPKD and ADPLD, not shown per patient.

nodes.description: Polycystin-1 is a very large, heavily N-glycosylated membrane protein whose maturation in the endoplasmic reticulum is rate-limiting for the polycystin complex. In Alg8-null renal epithelial cells polycystin-1 is hypoglycosylated, its steady-state level falls without any change in Pkd1 transcript, and the endoglycosidase H-resistant fraction that has passed the medial Golgi is markedly reduced. Re-expression of Alg8 rescues polycystin-1 expression. Other membrane proteins (polycystin-2, Na+/K+-ATPase, calnexin) were not quantitatively reduced, so the defect is relatively selective for polycystin-1.

nodes.description: Germline heterozygous loss-of-function variants, predominantly nonsense, frameshift and canonical splice alleles with recurrent p.Arg364*, reduce the dose of ALG8. ALG8 is the endoplasmic-reticulum alpha-1,3-glucosyltransferase that adds the second glucose to the dolichol-linked Glc1Man9GlcNAc2 precursor before the oligosaccharide is transferred to nascent glycoproteins. Unlike PRKCSH and SEC63, ALG8 is not intolerant of loss of function in the general population, which fits the incomplete penetrance of this disease.

nodes.description: Polycystin-1 is absent or markedly reduced in the primary cilia of Alg8-null cells. Cyst formation across the ADPKD/ADPLD gene family follows the amount of functional polycystin-1, which mouse genetics established for the ADPLD genes Prkcsh and Sec63 as a dose-response relationship. ALG8 is one of the endoplasmic-reticulum effectors whose loss feeds into that shared dosage mechanism.

In the unselected Mayo Clinic Biobank about half of carriers met an ADPKD cyst-number threshold, kidneys were usually not enlarged, and an atypical imaging pattern (asymmetric, few large cysts, or parenchymal atrophy) was common. Kidney function is usually preserved and kidney failure is rare.

nodes.description: Polycystic liver disease is thought to need a somatic second hit on top of the germline variant. In one ALG8 patient's explanted liver, ALG8 protein was absent from the cholangiocytes lining cysts but present in hepatocytes away from them, consistent with focal loss of the remaining allele. This is a single-case observation; the somatic lesion itself was not sequenced.
